findings.title: Blocking: every outbound credential resolution scans the retained identity table
findings.rationale: The newly introduced ChannelCredentialResolver.resolve loads providerIdentities through the reverse current_channel_id relation (api-app/src/domain/channels/channel-credential-resolver.ts:24-27) and selects the identity in memory at line36. That relation is not indexed: schema.prisma:252-270 and the foundation migration at lines100-115 define only the identity primary key, the provider/external_resource_id unique key and a bu_id index; the later admitted migrations add a cleanup_state/provider index, never current_channel_id. The parent channel primary-key lookup and the foreign-key declaration do not index this reverse lookup. Consequently the resolver's identity query must inspect the global provider_resource_identities table to find the attached row, including indefinitely retained tombstones from other BUs. This is on each BFF/public response send (conversations.service.ts:207) and each eligible Typebot execution (incoming.service.ts:81), also registration/verification, rather than only an administrative cleanup path. Returned cardinality near one does not bound scanned work. This is a concrete newly introduced O(all retained identities) database access on the message path and meets the dispatch's unbounded-scan blocker criterion; no production latency or saturation reproduction is claimed. D-07's durable ownership must remain intact and D-08 requires this shared resolver, but neither approves an unindexed reverse scan. The current EPS EXPLAIN tests only the attempt idempotency key (number-onboarding-pcv.e2e-spec.ts:30-34); its 25-row plan and GET timings cannot validate or exclude this different access path.
findings.suggested_action: Fix within the current contract before accepting the performance/EPS gate. Prefer resolving the channel's exact provider/externalResourceId through the existing composite unique key and checking currentChannelId, buId and managedLifecycle, avoiding the inverse collection entirely. Alternatively add a schema-backed, versioned migration index on current_channel_id and keep the same ownership/trust checks. Do not remove tombstones, add a cache or relax tenant/generation predicates. Preserve the caller and acceptance tests, and add discriminating query-plan/query-log evidence for the actual resolver path with a material population of unrelated retired identities so an attempt-only EXPLAIN cannot mask a regression. Repeat only the checks affected by the chosen correction; unchanged FRC/BCI/RLS observations remain usable subject to source freshness.
